what: A player enters an online Quantum match as a Genesis declared by token id; bots are Genesis of the roster.
build_status_detail: WebGL build finished. Genesis roster: 553 heroes, 3 of 3 roles with a character, ruleset genesis-0.2.0, asset [065760736FC09D1D].
method: node tools/unity/qualify_webgl.mjs in headless Chrome (software WebGL), Party Menu, Create, Start, then the on-screen stick pushed up for 4.5 s (CHOG_BROWSER_DRAG).
observed: Selection screen: only the Knight button remains and it is disabled; the team slot reads 'CHOG #1287 - Knight'.
In the match the local character is labelled 'CHOG #1287' with 6000 health (the Knight).
A bot of the same team is labelled 'CHOG #313'.
No 'Unable to find asset' warning in the browser console.

tests.simulation: python3 tools/quantum/headless.py test: 30 catalog checks and 18 Quantum tests passed, including three on the Genesis cast in a real Frame

defect_found_and_fixed.symptom: First build (20261009T054141817Z): the match logged 'Unable to find asset [065760736FC09D1D] (Quantum.GenesisRoster)' 81 times and silently used the sample cast.
defect_found_and_fixed.cause: Quantum registers a new asset in its database on a delayed Editor call; the build started before that call ran.
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: GenesisRosterImporter now checks the roster is registered, forces a database refresh otherwise, and fails the build request if it is still missing. The build status records which roster was embedded.

limits: The token id is a declaration typed in the URL: no wallet is connected and ownership is not checked.
One client and software rendering: no second device, no phone, no performance meaning.
Only one bot label was captured on screen; the uniqueness of bot Genesis in a match is covered by the simulation test, not observed here.
The roster holds 553 of 1,969 Genesis: those whose metadata is recorded. The others cannot enter a match yet.
Shape, effect and expression are carried by the character but no signature is implemented.
Starting the Gameplay scene directly in the Editor uses its local config, which has no roster.
